title: Trump Is Reopening the Middle East’s Deadliest Sectarian Fault Lines
gist: Hekmat Aboukhater argues the Trump administration's push to disarm Iraq's Shiite militias on a deadline and to have Syria's Sharaa 'take care of Hezbollah' risks reigniting Sunni-Shiite conflict across Iraq, Syria and Lebanon. With the Iran war already destabilizing the Gulf, U.S.-Saudi strikes on PMF positions, Yemen's truce collapsed and the Houthis controlling the Bab el-Mandeb, he urges rebuilt regional expertise and a restrained, locally negotiated approach.

insights.claim: Washington pressed Iraq's Trump-favored Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi to disarm Shiite armed factions by Sept. 30, but the militias refused, and Zaidi has extended the deadline to June 2027 while calling disarmament non-negotiable.
insights.speaker: Hekmat Aboukhater
insights.so_what: A prolonged armed standoff in Iraq is a latent risk to Iraqi oil output and the stability of a major OPEC producer.
insights.quote: That day has come and gone, and the militias refused to disarm.
insights.locator: Washington is now leaning on Ali al-Zaidi

insights.claim: Iraqi Shiite militias resist disarmament partly for material reasons, since their weapons sustain patronage networks, salaries, contracts and political leverage that would shrink if they demobilized.
insights.speaker: Hekmat Aboukhater
insights.so_what: Economic stakes make voluntary militia disarmament unlikely, implying persistent state-capacity and governance risk in Iraq.
insights.quote: Their weapons sustain patronage networks, salaries, contracts, and political leverage that would shrink if they demobilized.
insights.locator: The militias have plenty of reasons

insights.claim: Grand Ayatollah Ali al-Sistani, 96, has never rescinded the 2014 'defensive jihad' fatwa that created the PMF nor said what it means after his death, a succession question hanging over Iraq's entire disarmament debate.
insights.speaker: Hekmat Aboukhater
insights.so_what: Sistani's succession is a key event risk for Iraqi political stability and militia legitimacy.
insights.quote: a succession question that hangs over the entire disarmament debate.

insights.claim: In July, U.S. and Saudi aircraft struck PMF positions across Iraq in response to drones launched from Iraqi territory at Saudi oil facilities, and several factions prepared retaliatory strikes on Saudi Arabia and U.S. bases before Badr leader Hadi al-Amiri talked them down.
insights.speaker: Hekmat Aboukhater
insights.so_what: Drone attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure from Iraq and near-miss retaliation show live tail risk to Gulf oil supply.
insights.locator: In July, U.S. and Saudi aircraft

insights.claim: Iraqi leaders including former Prime Minister Nouri al-Maliki warn that forcing militia disarmament could trigger an internal confrontation that spills into neighboring countries, following the arrest of senior militia leader Abbas al-Yaqoubi.
insights.speaker: Hekmat Aboukhater
insights.so_what: Escalation risk in Iraq could widen regional conflict and disrupt energy flows.

insights.claim: Shiite political culture's mazlumiyah, a collective memory of being wronged from Hussein ibn Ali's martyrdom to Saddam-era repression and Islamic State massacres, makes U.S. disarmament demands resonate as threats in Baghdad.
insights.speaker: Hekmat Aboukhater
insights.so_what: Explains why coercive Western policy toward Shiite groups tends to harden rather than resolve resistance.
insights.locator: That distrust stems from something deeper

insights.claim: Syria scholar Joshua Landis frames the region's turmoil as the 'Great Sorting-Out,' the violent unwinding of the post-Sykes-Picot order as communities retreat into rigid ethnic and sectarian enclaves, with Iraq, Syria and Lebanon paying the highest price.
insights.speaker: Hekmat Aboukhater
insights.so_what: Suggests Levant instability is structural and long-duration, not a cyclical flare-up.

insights.claim: Sectarian violence remains fresh in the Levant: last year's massacre of more than 1,400 Syrian Alawites and killings of Druze in Suwayda threatened to unravel the new Syrian state, and at least 18 mass graves have been documented in Syria this year.
insights.speaker: Hekmat Aboukhater
insights.so_what: Ongoing sectarian violence undercuts Syria's post-Assad reconstruction and investment prospects.
insights.locator: Last year’s massacre of more than 1,400

insights.claim: U.S. policy across decades, from backing Saddam against Iran to supporting Saudi Arabia in Bahrain and Yemen, has reinforced a regional narrative of a U.S.-backed Sunni order versus Shiite challengers.
insights.speaker: Hekmat Aboukhater
insights.so_what: This perception constrains U.S. ability to act as a neutral broker in Shiite-majority states like Iraq.
insights.quote: a U.S.-backed Sunni order squaring off against Shiite challengers.

insights.claim: The Trump White House fired Nate Swanson, one of the few officials who deeply understood Iran and Shiite politics, depleting expertise just as it rolls out policies that risk a new sectarian unraveling.
insights.speaker: Hekmat Aboukhater
insights.so_what: Thin policy expertise raises the risk of U.S. miscalculation in Middle East crises.

insights.claim: Washington has suggested Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa's forces could 'take care of Hezbollah,' despite Syrian officials reportedly fearing it would ignite sectarian tensions in both countries.
insights.speaker: Hekmat Aboukhater
insights.so_what: Using proxies to coerce rivals raises the odds of a wider Levant war.
insights.locator: Across the border, Washington has pushed

insights.claim: Iran-aligned Iraqi Shiite factions warned Sharaa that any move against Hezbollah would be a declaration of war, meaning a Syrian intervention in Lebanon could mobilize Lebanese Sunnis behind Damascus while pulling Iraqi factions into the fight.
insights.speaker: Hekmat Aboukhater
insights.so_what: Maps a concrete escalation pathway linking Lebanon, Syria and Iraq into one conflict theater.

insights.claim: Hezbollah's Naim Qassem says the group's weapons are an internal Lebanese matter and it would only discuss folding them into national defense once the south is protected from Israeli incursions, while Israeli forces still occupy large parts of southern Lebanon.
insights.speaker: Hekmat Aboukhater
insights.so_what: Hezbollah disarmament is unlikely near term, keeping Lebanon's sovereign and reconstruction prospects impaired.
insights.quote: Nobody outside Lebanon has anything to do with the weapons
insights.locator: The situation is even more combustible

insights.claim: In the first weeks of the latest regional war roughly a million people fled their homes in Lebanon, with more than 200,000 crossing into Syria in March alone, according to the U.N. Refugee Agency.
insights.speaker: Hekmat Aboukhater
insights.so_what: Renewed communal violence could send refugee waves through Jordan and Turkey toward Europe, feeding European political risk.
insights.locator: This fire has already been lit.

insights.claim: The Iran war has destabilized Gulf Sunni-Shiite ties: Bahrain restricted Shiite observances, arrested clerics and barred mourning of Iran's late supreme leader, while Kuwait revoked thousands of citizenships and tightened rules on Shiite gatherings.
insights.speaker: Hekmat Aboukhater
insights.so_what: Rising internal sectarian repression adds social-stability risk in Gulf states.
insights.locator: Across the Gulf, the war in Iran

insights.claim: Yemen's four-year truce has broken, and in recent weeks the Iran-backed Houthis have taken most of the country's western coast and now fully control the Bab el-Mandeb strait.
insights.speaker: Hekmat Aboukhater
insights.so_what: Houthi control of the Bab el-Mandeb is a major risk to Red Sea shipping, oil tanker routes and freight rates.
insights.quote: the Iran-backed group has taken most of the country’s western coast and now fully controls the Bab el-Mandeb strait.

insights.claim: Sunni clerics accused the Houthis of attacking Mecca, though the group said it had targeted Aramco facilities instead.
insights.speaker: Hekmat Aboukhater
insights.so_what: Houthi strikes on Aramco infrastructure point to direct threats to Saudi oil supply.
insights.quote: Sunni clerics accused the Houthis of attacking Mecca, even though the group said it had targeted Aramco facilities instead.

insights.claim: The author recommends Washington rebuild regional expertise, stop imposing disarmament on deadlines, avoid using one regional actor to coerce another, and give Iraqi and Lebanese institutions space to negotiate sustainable arrangements.
insights.speaker: Hekmat Aboukhater
insights.so_what: Absent such a shift, the base case is elevated sectarian escalation risk across the Middle East.
